newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf producers warned of developing storm.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf producers warned of developing storm.

text.p: Offshore oil and natural gas producers operating in the Gulf of Mexico were warned on Wednesday to monitor a tropical disturbance showing signs of strengthening into a more severe storm, meteorologists said.

The National Hurricane Center planned to fly a weather plane through the low pressure system, which was generating strong winds and thunderstorms off the coast of Louisiana as it drifted slowly north-northeast, meteorologists said.
"It may be designated as a tropical depression before the day is over," Houston-based Wilkens Weather Service meteorologist John Springer said.

The system's convection, circular winds characteristic of tropical depressions and larger storms, intensified over the past 24 hours as it drifted over waters with surface temperatures ranging from 85 degrees F to 88 degrees F, he said.
The storm has not affected shipping and no warnings were raised for mariners, a U.S. Coast Guard spokeswoman said.
